transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… yeah, thank you for seeing me. I guess I’ve been trying to handle it, and maybe it’s not as bad as I’m making it sound, but… I keep getting these moments where I’m just suddenly back there.

It’s the scene with my cousin on the pavement. I can hear the shouting again, see the lights, like it’s happening right in front of me—even if I’m just standing in the church office trying to act normal. It kind of hits me out of nowhere. Does that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been experiencing these sudden moments of being back at the scene with your cousin?

It’s been… pretty much since it happened. My cousin was killed about two years and three months ago now, and these moments started after that. I guess I kept thinking they’d fade if I just stayed busy, but they’re still there.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened to your cousin?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make a big deal out of it, but I guess I do.

I’ll take the long way around town so I don’t have to pass the community center, or that court nearby. It probably sounds kind of silly, but if I’m already having a hard day, I just… I don’t want to see it.

And if people start talking about that night, I usually shut it down pretty quickly or find some reason to step out. I try to be polite about it, but I just don’t want to go there.
Do you have trouble sleeping at night?

Um… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I sleep sometimes. I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

Some nights are fine enough, I guess, and other nights I’m just… not really settled. But I don’t know if I’d call it “trouble sleeping” in the way you mean. Is there a specific kind of sleep problem you’re asking about?
Do you find yourself jumping or being easily startled by loud noises or unexpected movements?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really paid attention to, anyway.

I mean, loud noises aren’t my favorite, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m jumping out of my skin or anything. Maybe if something is really sudden, like anyone would react, but I haven’t thought of it as a major thing. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for what happened to your cousin?

Yeah… I mean, I know logically people tell me it wasn’t my fault. I don’t want to sound like I’m arguing with that.

But I do go over it a lot. I keep thinking if I had ended things earlier, or walked him out myself, or just kept a better eye on those boys… maybe he’d still be here.

I know that may not be fair to say, but it’s hard not to feel like I missed something I was supposed to do.
Do you often feel that you're a bad person or that you're worthless because of what happened to your cousin?

I… I don’t know if I’d say I’m worthless exactly. That sounds harsh, and I know I’m not supposed to talk about myself that way.

But most days there’s this… weight in my chest, like fear and anger and guilt all mixed together. From the time I wake up, I feel like I failed God, and my family, and the kids who trusted me. I know maybe that’s not the same as being a bad person, but it feels close sometimes.
Do you find it harder to feel happy or loving feelings towards people or things you used to enjoy since your cousin's death?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I don’t care about people or anything, because I do.

But things I used to really love just don’t feel the same. Preaching used to feel… alive to me. Playing keys, taking pictures, running with the guys on the court — those were things that filled me up. Now I either avoid them or I just kind of do them because I’m supposed to.

It’s like I’m there, but I’m not really in it. I don’t know if that answers it right, but… yeah, it’s harder to feel that joy like I used to.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy before your cousin's death that you still find pleasure in?

Honestly… not really like before.

I mean, I still try sometimes. I’ll sit at the keys or show up around the guys, or I’ll do what I need to do with preaching, but it doesn’t feel alive in me the way it used to. Taking pictures, playing, being on the court… those used to give me something back.

Now a lot of times I either avoid it, or I’m there but I’m just kind of going through the motions. I wish I could say there’s one thing that still feels the same, but… I don’t know. Not really.
Do you feel like you're unable to feel any strong emotions at all, even when something good happens?

I don’t know if I’d say I can’t feel anything at all… I mean, that sounds pretty extreme, and I don’t want to overstate it.

But even when something should feel good, it’s like it doesn’t really reach me the way it used to. Preaching, playing keys, taking pictures, running with the guys on the court — those used to really stir something in me. Now I mostly just go through the motions, or I avoid it altogether, because it doesn’t feel alive in me anymore.

Does that make sense? Like… I know something is supposed to be good, but I don’t really feel it strong.
Are there any activities that you have completely stopped doing since your cousin's death?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d say completely with everything, but there are things I’ve pretty much stopped doing unless I have to.

Like taking pictures — I don’t really pick up the camera the way I used to. And playing keys… I might sit down sometimes, but it’s not like before. Same with getting on the court with the guys. I’ll tell myself I’m busy or just not show up.

Preaching is harder to say because I still have responsibilities, but even there, a lot of the time I’m just going through the motions. None of it really feels alive in me anymore. Is that… is that what you mean?
Are there any activities that you've significantly reduced or lost interest in since your cousin's death?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve just quit everything, because I still try to show up where I’m supposed to.

But preaching used to mean a lot to me, and playing keys too. Taking pictures, running with the guys on the court… those were things I actually looked forward to. Since my cousin died, I’ve pulled back from a lot of it. Or if I do it, I’m kind of just there, going through the motions.

It just doesn’t feel alive in me like it used to. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Are there things you used to find very enjoyable that you've lost most of your interest in since your cousin passed away?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s fair to say.

I used to really love preaching, playing keys, taking pictures, and getting out on the court with the guys. Those things used to give me something, you know? Like they felt meaningful, or fun, or just… alive.

Now I either avoid them, or if I do show up, I’m mostly just going through the motions. I don’t want to make it sound like I don’t care about anything, but it’s just not there the same way anymore. Does that answer what you’re asking?

Yeah… I think I have, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I still try to do what I’m supposed to do, but… preaching used to really matter to me. Playing keys, taking pictures, running with the guys on the court — those were things I actually loved.

Now it’s like I either avoid them, or if I’m there, I’m just kind of going through the motions. It doesn’t feel alive in me the way it used to. Does that make sense?

Preaching used to feel really alive to me. Playing keys, taking pictures, even just running with the guys on the court — those were things I loved. Now a lot of the time I either don’t want to do them at all, or if I do, I’m just kind of there… going through the motions.

It’s not that I’m trying not to care. It just doesn’t feel the same in me anymore, if that makes sense.

Yeah… I know I kind of said it already, but yes.

Yeah… I guess the honest answer is yes. I don’t want it to sound like I’ve just given up on everything, but preaching used to mean a lot to me. Playing keys, taking pictures, running with the guys on the court… I really used to enjoy all of that.
